title: Product charter document
description: Tier-P product charter (doc 11 §6): the why/what root of a project. Narrative canonical form (.md): YAML frontmatter (envelope) + a personas data block + required markdown sections. Authored by the intake agent from the creation conversation and grounded in it (meta.source required). All downstream architecture and implementation walks back to this document.

type.description: Selects this schema. MUST be the literal string "product-charter".

source.description: Conversation grounding (Tier P requirement, doc 11 §4): at least one transcript span this charter was distilled from, so the user's words are traceable. Provide one entry per contributing run. Item shape matches the envelope's meta.source.

run.description: The Run id (02 §2) whose transcript this content was drawn from.

span.description: Optional locator within the transcript, e.g. "messages 12-31".

personas.description: The people this product serves. List every distinct persona the charter reasons about; user-workflows later reference these by id. At least one persona is required.

id.description: Stable persona identifier, PER-NNNN (e.g. PER-0001). MUST be unique within this charter; downstream documents cite it.

name.description: Short human-readable label for the persona (e.g. "Solo backend engineer"). One line, no markdown.

description.description: Who this persona is, their goals, and their context, in prose. Markdown allowed.

vision.description: The desired future state this product brings about: what the world looks like when it succeeds. Markdown.

problem.description: The problem being solved and why it matters now — the pain, who feels it, and the cost of the status quo. Markdown.

success-criteria.description: How success is judged: the observable outcomes or measures that, if met, mean the product worked. Markdown (a list is typical).

non-goals.description: What this product explicitly does NOT do — scope boundaries the team commits to, to prevent drift. Markdown (a list is typical).
